paragraphs.text: See on 2Ki 25:1.
paragraphs.anchor: In the ninth year of Zedekiah.

paragraphs.text: He came to the siege in person, but soon after retired himself to Riblah, i.e., to Antioch in Syria, there to take his pleasure, and therehence to send supplies to his forces as need required.
paragraphs.anchor: Came Nebuchadnezzar.

paragraphs.text: See on 2Ki 25:2. The sacking of Jerusalem occured four hundred and nineteen years after the building of the temple, (1004 to 588 BC) in the forty-seventh Olympiad, and when Tarquinius Priseus was king of Rome.
paragraphs.anchor: And in the eleventh year.

paragraphs.text: See on 2Ki 25:4.
paragraphs.anchor: The city was broken up.

paragraphs.text: Called the second gate (Zep 2:10; see Jer 1:15). Jeremiah lived to see many of his prophecies fulfilled. Jerusalem was taken in or about the fortieth year of his prophesying, as it was afterwards by the Romans, in or about the fortieth year after our Saviour’s ministry started.
paragraphs.anchor: In the middle gate.

paragraphs.text: Here we have a list of the Babylonian princes who first broke into the city. Their names are harsh and barbarous (such as are now to our ears the Turkish Bashaws, Beglerbegs, Sanzacks, &c.), but good enough for such to hear as would not yield to the sweet name and counsel of a gracious God. Those names that have Sar or Rab in them are deemed to be names of office; as Sarezer, master of the treasures; Rabinag, master of the magicians, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: Even Nergalsharezer, Shamgarnebo.

paragraphs.text: Not entered, but ready to enter. See 2Ki 25:4.
paragraphs.anchor: When Zedekiah the king saw them.

paragraphs.text: Intending likely for Egypt; but his journey was shortened. So was Muliasses, king of Tunis, when fleeing from his son Amidas, he was discovered by the sweet perfumes he had about him; and being brought back, had, like Zedekiah, his eyes put out with a burning hot iron.
paragraphs.anchor: He went out the way of the plain.

paragraphs.text: See on 2Ki 25:5.
paragraphs.anchor: But the Chaldeans pursued.

paragraphs.text: See on 2Ki 25:6-7.
See on 2Ki 25:7.
See on 2Ki 25:8.
See on 2Ki 25:11-12.

See on 2Ki 25:11-12. Sic vides miras rerum vices. See what a wonderful turn of things was here on the sudden, and how that of Seneca was here made good, Una dies interest inter magnam civitatem et nullam, There is but a day’s difference sometimes between a great city and no city. Josephus and some others say that the Rechabites, as men peaceable, and given much to contemplation, were also left in the land. This destruction of Jerusalem was, saith Oecolampadius, a kind of type of the general judgment. For like as in Jerusalem the wicked perished, but the poor and peaceable were not only spared, but enriched, so shall it be at that day.

Now Nebuchadnezzar … gave charge, &c.] He had heard of Jeremiah and his preaching by those Jews that, by the prophet’s persuasion, fell to the Chaldees; and now that promise took place, I will cause the enemy to entreat thee well: {Jer 15:11}
“ Tandem bona causa triumphat. ”
A wicked man, we see, may be loving and liberal to a godly minister for self ends. Let no man, therefore, rest in it alone as a sure sign of an honest man.
paragraphs.anchor: Take him, and look well to him.

paragraphs.text: These, who before were so active in destroying the city, are now no less active in honouring the good prophet. All things work together for good to the godly: their greatest enemies shall one day do them honour.
paragraphs.anchor: So Nebuzaradan, &c.

paragraphs.text: But why did they not also loose him from his bonds? {Jer 40:1}
paragraphs.anchor: They sent and took Jeremiah.

paragraphs.text: Who being a chieftain among the Jews, fell to the Chaldees (as it may seem) before the city was taken, according to Jeremiah’s counsel, and is now set over the land, and hath the prophet Jeremiah committed to his care.
paragraphs.anchor: And committed him unto Gedaliah.

paragraphs.text: Who had rescued the prophet. {Jer 26:24} {See Trapp on "Jer 26:24"}
paragraphs.anchor: The son of Ahikam.

paragraphs.text: Which is never bound, {2Ti 2:9} but runneth and is glorified. {2Th 3:1}
paragraphs.anchor: Now the word of the Lord.

paragraphs.text: Who yet was an Israelite indeed by his faith and religion, as was likewise Jether the Ishmaelite. {1Ch 7:17 2Sa 17:25}
paragraphs.anchor: Go and speak unto Ebedmelech the Ethiopian.

paragraphs.text: Who will not fail to give, unto him who showeth kindness to any prophet of his, a prophet’s reward. {Mat 10:41-42}
paragraphs.anchor: Thus saith the Lord of hosts.

paragraphs.text: See Jer 20:16; Jer 44:27.
paragraphs.anchor: Behold, I will bring my words upon this city for evil.

paragraphs.text: Thou shalt see it, but shalt survive it. And this prophecy may be unto us instead of a most certain history.
paragraphs.anchor: And they shall be accomplished in that day before thee.

paragraphs.text: From the sword, the famine, and the pestilence. "A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand, but it shall not come nigh thee; only with thine eyes shalt thou behold and see the reward of the wicked"; {Psa 91:7-8} and that the Lord is sure, though slow, tarditatem supplicii gravitate compensans. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: But I will deliver thee in that day.

paragraphs.text: Zedekiah’s courtiers, who do bear thee an aching tooth for thy kindness to my prophet, and have vowed revenge.
paragraphs.anchor: And thou shalt not be delivered into the hands of those men.

paragraphs.text: {a} Val. Max.

Heb., Delivering, deliver thee. It would be a great stay of mind, if God should say the same to us in particular and by name, as he doth here to this Ethiopian. And yet he saith no less to us in the precious promises, which we are by faith to appropriate.
paragraphs.anchor: For I will surely deliver thee.

paragraphs.text: Pro lucre cessura est. For saving my prophet’s life, thou shall have thine own; so sure a gain is godliness.
paragraphs.anchor: But thy life shall be for a prey unto thee.

paragraphs.text: What may not faith have at God’s hands? Those that trust him, do, after a sort, engage him to deliver them, and to do them good.
paragraphs.anchor: Because thou hast put thy trust in me.
